name: shortn_v2
description: Shortn is a comprehensive link management solution that goes beyond simple URL shortening. It provides powerful analytics, customizable QR codes, and beautiful link-in-bio pages—all in one platform.

paragraphs: This starts the new web app at redirects on port 3002, API on 3003, and worker on 3004. It loads .env.staging explicitly, maps the legacy MONGODBKEY to the new database settings, and uses localhost for app/auth origins. Optional OAuth providers require valid credential pairs; unavailable providers are reported at startup.

Missing Redis URLs use dedicated Docker services on ports 16380 (cache) and 16379 (durable). Missing MongoDB settings use a local replica set on port 27020. When all S3 settings are absent, the launcher starts local RustFS storage on port 19000 and creates the development bucket. Explicit remote connections, including the S3 settings in .env.staging, are preserved. Missing link and confirmation signing keys are derived for local development from BETTERAUTHSECRET. The launcher does not modify .env.staging or run database migrations.

QR logos, account avatars and bio images upload directly from files. The server validates images (up to 5 MB), converts them to PNG and stores them in S3. Replacing or removing an image changes the saved reference; existing objects are retained.
features: Shorten URLs with custom, branded links
Track engagement with real-time analytics and insights
Generate QR codes with full customization options
Build link-in-bio pages that showcase all your important links in one place
Organize campaigns and measure performance across channels

requirements.text: Email checks capture Resend payloads on a local HTTP receiver, follow generated approval/verification links, check expired/used links and session revocation, and sign in with the updated address.
Neither command contacts Polar or creates charges; live provider flows still need staging verification.
Pass --billing-only for the focused billing checks, or --mutations-only to skip the locale route sweep while retaining browser mutations and cross-service checks.
